title: interactive-inference-playground-prd-2028-02-15
author: Asha Patel
content:
Title: Interactive Inference Playground (PRD)

Summary
-------
The Interactive Inference Playground is a first-class, in-Console tool that lets developers and platform engineers compose realistic inference scenarios and immediately see model, deployment, cost, and latency tradeoffs. The Playground provides an executable sandbox for: trying prompts against model variants, simulating batching and KV cache hit rates, toggling quantization and routing rules, and exporting validated configuration bundles for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Why this matters
------------------
- Lowers time-to-experiment for engineers evaluating tradeoffs between latency, cost, and quality.
- Reduces costly mistakes when moving from PoC to production by letting teams validate behavior under representative traffic shapes.
- Improves onboarding: demo-ready examples reduce friction for new accounts and enable self-serve migration paths to Dedicated or Private deployments.

Goals (measurable)
------------------
1. Provide a UI and API that can simulate 80% of common production scenarios (per customer survey) within the first release.
2. Enable export of a deployment-ready config (runtime + routing + rollout policy) that passes Redwood automated validation checks for Dedicated/Private deployments.
3. Reduce sandbox-to-production rollout surprises: target < 10% post-rollout rollback rate for customers who use an exported Playground config for their first rollout.
4. Achieve a 25% increase in self-serve conversions (trial -> paid) for accounts that use the Playground during trial.

Non-goals
---------
- Full fidelity offline performance emulation of every GPU hardware variant (we will provide representative profiles and conservative estimates).
- Replacing existing load-testing tools; Playground is focused on scenario composition and light-weight simulation, not high-load stress tests.

User personas and primary flows
------------------------------
- Developer (fast iteration): write a prompt, select model variant, toggle streaming/stop conditions, view immediate token-level latency and cost estimate.
- ML Engineer / Platform Engineer (validation): define traffic shape (qps, burst), prefix KV cache hit rate, batching policy, and observe percentile latency and cost curves. Export validated config for Dedicated or Private.
- Solutions/SE (demo): switch prebuilt scenarios to demonstrate cost/latency differences for customers.

User stories
------------
1. As a developer I can paste a prompt and get a side-by-side comparison of two model variants showing expected median latency and cost per 1k tokens.
2. As an ML engineer I can define a workload profile and see how different batching window sizes and cache hit rates affect p95 latency.
3. As an admin I can export a validated configuration bundle (model variant pinning, fallback rules, batching hints, rollout policy) that is annotated with validation warnings and estimated monthly cost.

Acceptance criteria
-------------------
- UI: Compose scenario panel, results panel with charts (latency percentiles, cost per token, token counts), and export button.
- API: /playground/simulate POST endpoint that returns a deterministic simulation report for given inputs.
- Export: Generated JSON bundle must pass the Redwood validation service with a pass/warn/fail summary.
- Tests: Automated E2E tests that run 30 representative scenarios and assert metrics are within expected ranges for the simulator.

Functional requirements (MUST)
-----------------------------
1. Scenario composition fields: model variant(s), prompt(s), sequence length distribution (sampled histogram), qps / burst pattern, KV cache hit rate, batching policy, quantization profile selection, streaming vs non-streaming.
2. Simulation engine: ingest scenario and produce: token-level cost estimate, latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) for a 10-minute simulated window, and an SLO risk score.
3. Comparison mode: allow up to three scenario variants compared side-by-side.
4. Export: produce a configuration bundle with metadata, constraints, and validation results; bundle should include a human-readable summary.
5. Permissions: visible to account admins and developers with Console write access; export requires admin role.

Functional requirements (SHOULD)
-------------------------------
1. Provide prebuilt scenario templates for common workloads: chat agent, embeddings ingestion, vector search query, short completion bursts.
2. Integrate with Console cost-estimates to surface monthly cost delta if used as production.
3. Allow saving named scenarios to account workspace for reuse and sharing.

Non-functional requirements
---------------------------
- Latency: Simulation API must return results for small scenarios (< 30 tokens, single variant) within 3s. Larger multi-variant scenarios should return within 20s with streaming progress updates.
- Scales: Playground backend must support 500 concurrent active simulations for the hosted Console with graceful backpressure.
- Security: No customer PII is retained by default; prompts are processed under the same data handling policies as the hosted API.

Design and architecture (high-level)
-----------------------------------
Components:
1. Playground Console UI: React-based single-page app embedded in Console.
2. Playground Orchestrator Service: stateless API that validates inputs, enqueues simulation jobs, and returns results.
3. Simulation Engine Pool: horizontally scalable fleet (K8s) running parameterized simulations using Redwood runtime profiles. Engine instances are sandboxed and use mocked backends for non-essential services.
4. Validation Service integration: exported bundles are sent to existing validation service (re-use) for Dedicated/Private compatibility checks.
5. Telemetry Collector: emits simulation metrics, cost estimates, and usage telemetry to Console analytics and Cost Warehouse.

Sequence (happy path)
---------------------
1. User opens Playground and selects or creates a scenario.
2. Console UI sends /playground/simulate to Orchestrator service.
3. Orchestrator schedules the job to Simulation Engine Pool.
4. Engine runs lightweight simulations using model performance profiles and returns per-token latency and cost estimates.
5. Orchestrator aggregates results, stores an ephemeral record for replay, and returns report to UI.
6. User optionally exports the validated bundle; orchestrator forwards bundle to Validation Service and updates UI with pass/warn/fail.

Simulation fidelity model
------------------------
- Use curated performance profiles for each model variant (median token latency, memory footprint, batch scaling curves).
- Inject conservative jitter and failure modes for realism (e.g., simulated cold-start + KV miss penalties).
- Allow advanced users to upload custom profile overrides for on-prem tests (requires security review).

Configuration examples (UI & API)
--------------------------------
Example API request payload (textual):
POST /playground/simulate
{
  "scenario_name": "chat-agent-high-qps",
  "models": ["redwood-rlm-7b-v2", "open-compat-7b-quant"],
  "seq_histogram": "{\"8-32\":0.6, \"33-128\":0.3, \"129-512\":0.1}",
  "qps": 120,
  "burst": 400,
  "kv_cache_hit_rate": 0.65,
  "batching_policy": {"max_batch_ms": 8, "preferred_batch_size": 32},
  "quant_profile": "int8-mixed",
  "duration_minutes": 10
}

Example export bundle (human readable excerpt):
- models: redwood-rlm-7b-v2 (primary), open-compat-7b-quant (fallback)
- batching_hint: max_batch_ms=8, preferred_size=32
- rollout: gradual canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with auto-fallback to fallback variant on p95 > 800ms
- estimated_monthly_tokens: 128M
- estimated_monthly_cost: $3,420 (hosted estimate)
- validation: WARN - fallback variant lacks exact streaming parity, expect small output variance

Telemetry, metrics and SLOs
--------------------------
- Usage metrics: scenarios_created, simulations_run_total, exports_generated, average_runtime_seconds.
- Business metrics: trial_accounts_using_playground, export_to_dedicated_rate.
- Simulation quality SLO: agreed baseline — 95% of simulator median latency predictions should be within +/- 20% of measured median in production for customers who opt-in to telemetry over first 30 days.

Security and data governance
----------------------------
- Prompts: default ephemeral retention of 24 hours; account admins can opt into longer retention for shared scenarios. Retention policy stored in account settings.
- Export bundles: may contain metadata about sample prompts; exports must be redacted if account-level PII redaction is enabled.
- Private deployments: exported bundles for Private must not include hosted-only resource identifiers; Validation Service will rewrite or reject invalid fields.

Rollout plan and milestones
--------------------------
Phase 0 — Prototype (Q2 2028)
- Internal MVP with 10 prebuilt scenarios and simulation engine using representative profiles.
- Internal dogfood with Solutions, SE, and a small set of trial customers.

Phase 1 — Public beta (Q3 2028)
- Console UI enabled for all trial accounts. Templates for chat, embeddings, search. Export disabled for Private/Dedicated (beta).
- Collect telemetry and run calibration against 15 pilot customers.

Phase 2 — GA (Q4 2028)
- Export enabled and integrated with Validation Service. Onboarding guides and templates published.
- Growth experiments: in-console contextual nudges and scenario suggestions.

Ownership and resourcing
------------------------
- Product: Asha Patel (PM) — overall feature owner.
- Eng: Runtime (lead: Daniel Kim) — simulation engine profiles & model integrations; Console UI (lead: Priya Nambiar).
- Design/UX: Marta Ruiz.
- Solutions/SE: Liam Zhang — pilot coordination and templates.
- Security/Privacy reviewer: Sinead O'Leary.

Dependencies and risks
---------------------
- Depend on accurate performance profiles from Eng-Serving-Runtime. Delays in benchmarking will reduce simulator fidelity.
- Validation Service must support additional bundle schemas; require small extension.
- Risk of over-promising fidelity: clearly label simulator as advisory and include confidence bands in UI.

Open questions
--------------
- Should exported bundles include suggested autoscaling policies, or leave autoscaling recommendations to Dedicated sales engineers?
- What is the long-term retention policy for saved scenarios on free vs paid tiers?
